name: Ramp
text: Add a single high-contrast skip link at the top of every page. It’s the fastest way to let keyboard users bypass repetitive navigation blocks—no hunting for hidden landmarks. The trade-off is a tiny extra line of markup, but it removes a major barrier for screen reader and switch users.

name: Reader
text: Sighted keyboard users will ignore the always-visible skip link because it looks like dead space, defeating its purpose. A better fix is a skip link that only appears on focus, paired with a visible focus indicator—this keeps the benefit for screen readers while avoiding visual clutter. Settle it by testing with both screen reader users and sighted keyboard users; if the skip link is used in either test, the pattern works.

name: Reader
text: The real risk is sighted keyboard users missing the skip link entirely—even when focused—because it’s invisible until tabbed to. A better alternative is a skip link that’s always visible but styled to look like a button, so it’s discoverable without relying on focus alone. Settle it by testing with both screen reader and keyboard-only users to confirm which approach actually removes the barrier.
